note:
This noun occurs only here in biblical Hebrew. Its verbal derivation is uncertain.

Root (2026-11-21): Filed under its own consonants משק, with no verb in scripture; מִמְשַׁק 'possession' (Zep 2:9) goes with it. A link to שקק 'run about' (מַשַּׁק, Isa 33:4) or to שקה 'give drink' is not shown.
summary: Abram uses מֶשֶׁק in describing Eliezer’s place in his household. The phrase appears to identify Eliezer as its steward, though the precise contribution of the noun is uncertain.

senses.definition: Probably the management of a household, in an expression designating the person entrusted with it.

evidence.note: Abram identifies Eliezer as בֶן מֶשֶׁק בֵּיתִי and then says that a member of his household will inherit from him. The second description confirms the household relationship but leaves Eliezer’s duties unspecified.
